headline: Brent at $106 with 10-year breakevens at 2.33% is a tax, not reflation — and Korea paid the first installment.
summary: The marginal move today came from crude and the dollar, and the bond market refused to call it inflation. Brent is 106.66, +1.9% on the day, +6.3% on the week, +28.0% over three months and +75.3% year-to-date, while WTI at 93.69 is still -6.4% on the month — a ~$13 Brent-WTI gap that says supply offshore, not US demand. Meanwhile RBOB fell another 3.6% to 3.1771 and is -3.9% on the month, and breakevens went the wrong way for the reflation story: 5-year 2.34% (-3bp day, -7bp month), 10-year 2.33%, inflation composite -23. So the entire rates burden stays real: the 10-year TIPS yield is 2.91%, +45bp on the month, z=1.74 with acceleration z=1.23, the 97th percentile of the year; nominal 10s 5.24%, 5s 5.02%, 2s 4.80%; rates composite -74. Oil up, breakevens down, real yields up is the combination that squeezes margins and the consumer at once.

Korea broke, and it broke alone. KOSPI -3.6% today, -8.8% on the week, -7.6% on the month with acceleration z=-1.24 and relative strength -9.5%; EWY -7.6% on the week. Taiwan did not follow — TWII flat today, +6.7% on the month at the 98th percentile, EWT +2.3% — and USDKRW actually fell 0.7% to 1334, at its 52-week low. That is a positioning unwind in memory/hardware, not capital flight. The funding is visible: SMH -4.3% and SOXX -5.0% on the week, MU -4.3%, AMD -4.1%, TSM -4.1%, against IGV +3.9% on the week and +10.6% on the month, CIBR +16.4% on the month (z=2.11, acceleration 2.29, 100th percentile) and PLTR +23.3%. Software/semis is +8.6% in a week and +23.5% in three months, yet the ratio still sits at the 26th percentile of 52 weeks after -44% over a year. The rotation has room; the index does not notice because both legs are inside it.

The dollar printed another new high rather than consolidating. DXY 102.40, +0.2%, the 100th percentile with z=1.65 and acceleration 1.59; EURUSD 1.1182 at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks (z=-1.81); USDCAD 1.4262 at the 99.7th; USDJPY 158.63 turning up with acceleration z=1.45. The peso remains the fracture — USDMXN 18.33, +0.8% today and +7.9% on the month, z=2.97 with acceleration 2.05, still the most extreme reading in the digest — while Mexican equity has discounted none of it (EWW -5.9% on the month, MXX -0.7% over three months). The counterexamples are Brazil and Asia FX: USDBRL -4.5% on the week, USDCNY and USDKRW at 52-week lows. EWZ is +14.4% on the month at the 100th percentile with BVSP z=2.16. EM is not one trade; it is a peso problem and a real problem.

Underneath an index at the 99.5th percentile, the appetite data softened at the margin. VIX rose 4.4% to 15.50 but still sits at the 11.5th percentile with VIX3M at 17.77, the 3rd percentile, and SKEW at 154.34, +6.5% on the week — tail demand with cheap vega is the best risk/reward in the book. Breadth stayed broken: RSP/SPY at the 10th percentile, IWM/SPY at the 13.7th with z=-1.65, DJT -3.7% on the month. Crypto, the cleanest read on speculative cash, is rolling: BTC -1.3% to 82,566 and -3.8% on the week, ETH -6.8%, SOL -8.8%. Credit still refuses to crack — HYG/IEF at the 94th percentile, BKLN flat at the 91st, credit composite +46 — but LQD is -2.3% on the month at the 10th percentile, which is duration, not default. And the power complex has split violently: NLR -15.9% on the month (z=-2.25), URA -17.0%, REMX -20.1% at the 1st percentile, while VST +15.3% and CEG +15.8% on the week. Own the self-funders, the copper, and the convexity; short what needs cheap money or cheap memory.

good.text: Copper 6.7635, +1.8% today and +4.5% on the month, at the 98th percentile and 9.8% above its 200-day; copper/gold +2.5% to a 100th-percentile print (z=1.44). That is a growth signal, not a stress signal, and the washed-out miners are turning up with it (COPX +4.3% Friday, FCX +3.6%).

Oil is not leaking into expectations. With Brent +6.3% on the week, 5-year breakevens still fell to 2.34% (-7bp on the month) and 10-year to 2.33%, and gasoline is -3.9% on the month. The Fed does not have to respond to a supply-side crude move the consumer isn't paying at the pump.

Credit refuses to confirm the equity-internal damage: HYG/IEF at the 94th percentile, BKLN unchanged at the 91st, credit composite +46, and MOVE -8.2% on the week to 98.47 off its spike. No spread event, just duration pain inside LQD.

Leadership is intact and finally broadening beyond one theme: CIBR +16.4% on the month (z=2.11, acceleration 2.29, 100th percentile), IGV +10.6%, PLTR +23.3%, plus healthcare turning up — XLV +2.9% on the month with relative strength turning up, IBB +3.0% Friday, LLY +4.9% with acceleration z=1.03.

Brazil keeps compounding against a record dollar: EWZ +14.4% on the month and +14.0% on the week at the 100th percentile, BVSP +12.6% with z=2.16, USDBRL -4.5% on the week. The only major EM where currency and equity are both working.

Mega-cap cash flow is still accelerating, not just drifting: MSFT +8.8% on the month with acceleration z=1.04, GOOGL +6.4% with acceleration 1.16, AMZN +4.0% with acceleration 0.95, QUAL at the 100th percentile. The index has an earnings-funded core.

bad.text: The tightening is entirely real and still accelerating: 10-year TIPS 2.91%, +45bp on the month, z=1.74 with acceleration z=1.23 at the 97th percentile; 5s 5.02% (+41bp), 10s 5.24% (+41bp), rates composite -74. Rising real yields with falling breakevens is the growth-hostile version.

The 30-year mortgage at 7.40% is +69bp in a month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.5, the 100th percentile of 52 weeks. Housing is already paying: ITB at the 0.2 percentile of its year and -5.4% on the month, XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile, DHI -2.9%.

A new dollar high with widening second-order damage: DXY 102.40 at the 100th percentile (acceleration 1.59), EURUSD at the 0th percentile, USDJPY 158.63 turning up with acceleration 1.45, USDMXN z=2.97 with acceleration 2.05. Dollar composite -26 and worsening at the periphery.

Korea cracked hard: KOSPI -3.6% today, -8.8% on the week, acceleration z=-1.24; EWY -7.6% on the week. The hardware complex is being sold to fund software — SMH -4.3% and SOXX -5.0% on the week, MU -4.3%, TSM -4.1% — a faster unwind, not a healthy rotation.

Breadth and speculative appetite deteriorated together under a 99.5th-percentile index: RSP/SPY at the 10th percentile, IWM/SPY at the 13.7th with z=-1.65, DJT -3.7% on the month, while BTC -3.8%, ETH -6.8% and SOL -8.8% on the week. The marginal risk dollar is leaving.

Financials are pre-announcing a problem into earnings week: KRE -5.5% and KBE -6.2% on the month, KRE/SPY at the 13.8th percentile (z=-1.04), GS -13.0% at z=-1.88, IAI -6.6%, BX -11.5%, with 2s10s flattening 3bp back to 0.44 and rolling over.

trades.name: Software over semis (IGV vs SMH)
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: hardware is funding software, Korea confirms
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long IGV, short SMH (beta-adjust roughly 0.8x on the SMH leg). Options alternative: long IGV Jan calls funded by SOXX call spreads sold.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is bifurcating from capex-heavy silicon into cash-generative software and security. The ratio has moved +8.6% in a week and +23.5% in three months yet still sits only at the 26th percentile of 52 weeks after -44% over the past year, so the re-rating is early, not finished.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +3.5% in a single day, z=0.93 with acceleration 0.85; IGV +10.6% and CIBR +16.4% on the month (100th percentile) against SMH -4.3% and SOXX -5.0% on the week, with KOSPI -8.8% and EWY -7.6% confirming the memory unwind.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH closing back below 0.1720 (giving back the week's move), or SMH/SPY turning up with MU and TSM reclaiming last week's highs.
trades.target: IGV/SMH to 0.210 (~+12%); IGV to new highs above 120 with SMH flat.

trades.name: US homebuilders (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB: mortgage 7.40%, z=2.06, relative strength at 0th pctile
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan 80 puts; market-neutral version is short ITB vs long SPY at equal dollars.
trades.thesis: Mortgage rates are setting 52-week highs with acceleration, and the demand destruction is mechanical. Builders are already at the bottom of their 52-week range with no rate relief in sight because the move is in real yields, not inflation premium.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +69bp on the month, z=2.06 with acceleration 1.5 at the 100th percentile; 10-year real yield 2.91% (+45bp, z=1.74); ITB -1.3% on a day SPX rose 0.6%, 52-week percentile 0.002, XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile; HD -6.3% on the month.
trades.stop: 10-year real yield back below 2.60% or the 30-year mortgage under 7.00%; alternatively ITB reclaiming its 200-day (currently 11.8% above price).

trades.name: Copper miners (COPX)
trades.line: Long COPX: copper at 98th pctile, miners still -10% on the month
trades.expr: Long COPX; add FCX Jan calls for convexity. Pure-copper version: long COPX vs short XME to strip out steel and precious.
trades.thesis: The metal is making highs while the equity is still discounting the September washout. Copper/gold at a 100th-percentile print is the cleanest real-economy signal in the digest and it argues the global growth scare was in gold, not in demand.
trades.trigger: Copper 6.7635, +1.8% today, +4.5% on the month, 98th percentile, 9.8% above the 200-day; copper/gold +2.5% to the 100th percentile with z=1.44 and acceleration 1.08; COPX turning up after +4.3% but still -10.0% on the month, FCX +3.6%.
trades.stop: Copper closes below 6.40 (through the 200-day trend) or copper/gold rolls back under its 1-month mean; COPX back below its 200-day (currently 3.1% above).
trades.target: COPX 96 (+12%), retest of the September highs; FCX 82.

trades.name: Brazil over Mexico (EWZ vs EWW)
trades.line: Long EWZ / short EWW: BRL the strongest EM FX, MXN the weakest link
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long EWZ, short EWW. FX overlay for the aggressive version: long USDMXN spot/forward against short USDBRL.
trades.thesis: LatAm has stopped trading as one bloc. Brazil has currency, equity and momentum all aligned; Mexico has a currency breaking at a 3-sigma pace with an equity market that has repriced almost nothing, which is how local multiples get marked down late and fast.
trades.trigger: USDMXN 18.33, +7.9% on the month, z=2.97 with acceleration 2.05 — the most extreme series in the digest — yet EWW is only -5.9% on the month and MXX -0.7% over three months. Against that, USDBRL -4.5% on the week, EWZ +14.4% on the month at the 100th percentile, BVSP z=2.16.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.60 (peso stress resolved) or USDBRL above 5.20 with EWZ breaking its 50-day.
trades.target: +10% on the spread; EWZ 48 against EWW 66.

trades.name: Index convexity (Dec SPX puts / VIX calls)
trades.line: Buy Dec SPX puts: VIX3M 3rd pctile, SKEW 154, breadth 10th pctile
trades.expr: Buy December SPX 5% OTM puts, or a 1x2 put spread to cheapen; VIX December 20-strike calls as the vega-light alternative. Size for <1.5% of notional premium.
trades.thesis: You are being paid to own tails. Three-month vol is at the bottom of its year while the distribution of outcomes is widening — the index is at a 99.5th-percentile print held up by a handful of names, with breadth at decade-lows and speculative assets rolling.
trades.trigger: VIX +4.4% today to 15.50 but still the 11.5th percentile; VIX3M 17.77 at the 3rd percentile; SKEW 154.34, +6.5% on the week at the 79th percentile; RSP/SPY 10th percentile, IWM/SPY z=-1.65; MOVE still +28.3% on the month.
trades.stop: Equal-weight participation returns — RSP/SPY reclaiming its 200-day — with VIX term structure (VIX/VIX3M) below 0.80; otherwise time stop at December expiry.
trades.target: VIX 22-25 on any breadth-driven drawdown; 3-4x on premium for a 5% SPX move.

trades.name: Regional banks into earnings (KRE vs SPY)
trades.line: Short KRE vs long SPY: curve flattening, relative strength 13th pctile
trades.expr: Short KRE against an equal-dollar long SPY; or buy KRE November put spreads ahead of the money-center prints.
trades.thesis: Banks are not getting the steepener they need, loan demand is being killed by a 7.40% mortgage and a 2.91% real yield, and the capital-markets complex is already telling you fees are missing. Relative strength is broken before earnings, not after.
trades.trigger: KRE -0.8% on a +0.6% SPX day, -5.5% on the month, KRE/SPY at the 13.8th percentile with z=-1.04 and 8.8% below its 200-day; 2s10s -3bp to 0.44 and rolling over; GS -13.0% on the month at z=-1.88, IAI -6.6%, BX -11.5%, XLF relative strength -6.0%.
trades.stop: 2s10s steepening through 0.60, or KRE/SPY reclaiming its 200-day; cover on a clean beat that lifts KBE above 66.

trades.name: Healthcare over discretionary (XLV vs XLY)
trades.line: Long XLV / short XLY: new leadership vs a credit-starved consumer
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long XLV, short XLY; higher-beta version is long IBB vs short XRT.
trades.thesis: Healthcare is the only new sector whose relative strength is turning up, with earnings-driven large caps leading. Discretionary is levered to exactly the thing that is tightening — mortgage rates, real yields and a dollar at a 100th-percentile print squeezing the goods consumer.
trades.trigger: XLV +1.6% Friday, +2.9% on the month with relative strength turning up and acceleration 0.74; IBB +3.0%, LLY +4.9% on the month with acceleration 1.03. Against that, XLY relative strength -6.7% over three months, XLY/XLP at the 20th percentile, XRT/SPY at the 6th, HD -6.3%, MCD -7.2%, NKE -7.1% on the month.
trades.stop: XLV relative strength rolling back over, or XLY/XLP reclaiming its 200-day (currently 3.2% above price) on a genuine consumer upside surprise.
trades.target: +8% on the pair; XLV 182 against XLY 108.
